title: Delineating Oxidation Aspects of an Additively Manufactured Nanoprecipitation-Strengthened Al<sub>0.2</sub>Co<sub>1.5</sub>CrFeNi<sub>1.5</sub>Ti<sub>0.3</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Nanoprecipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloy powder with nominal composition Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 produced for laser powder-bed fusion.
recollection.intervention: Additive manufacturing (LPBF) to build bulk coupons, followed by isothermal oxidation tests in air between ~800 °C and 1100 °C and post-exposure microstructural/chemical characterization (SEM/TEM, EDS, XRD, TGA).
recollection.structure: As-built material shows an FCC matrix containing ~20–50 nm L12-type (Al,Ti)-rich nanoprecipitates; after oxidation, a duplex external scale composed mainly of Cr2O3 + Al2O3 with scattered TiO2/spinel particles forms, underlain by a precipitation-hardened FCC core that coarsens slightly but retains nanoscale precipitates.
recollection.mechanism: Selective outward diffusion of Cr and Al during high-temperature exposure generates a continuous Cr2O3/Al2O3 layer that slows further oxygen ingress; fine precipitates and high defect density from LPBF accelerate Al supply to the surface, while Ti partitions to the oxide, forming TiO2 and promoting spinel formation at the scale/substrate interface.
recollection.results: Parabolic oxidation rate constants kp ~3×10⁻¹² g² cm⁻⁴ s⁻¹ at 900 °C and ~1×10⁻¹¹ g² cm⁻⁴ s⁻¹ at 1000 °C, roughly 3–5× lower than cast/wrought counterparts. Mass gain after 100 h at 1000 °C ≈1.2 mg cm⁻² versus ≈3 mg cm⁻² for a similar composition without nanoprecipitation strengthening. Mechanical testing after 100 h oxidation shows yield strength retention of ~85 % of as-built value (~1 GPa → ~850 MPa).

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies additive manufacturing and subsequent isothermal oxidation, but misses the central comparison between as-printed and 750°C/50 h aged states and gives an incorrect temperature range. Its structural account wrongly places L12 precipitates in the as-built material and mischaracterizes the oxide as a Cr2O3/Al2O3 duplex rather than the observed Cr-rich protective layer plus discontinuous inner Al/Ti-rich region. The mechanism correctly notes that Cr2O3 limits oxygen ingress, but the proposed continuous Al2O3 contribution and precipitate-assisted Al transport are unsupported. All reported rate constants, mass gains, comparisons, and strength-retention numbers are absent from or inconsistent with the actual results.
